metric: AUROC of the ECGFounder foundation model across diagnoses on internal/external validation, and fine-tuned performance vs baseline models
result: AUROC >0.95 for 80 diagnoses on internal validation with strong generalization on external sets; fine-tuned model outperformed baseline methods by 3-5 AUROC points across demographic analysis, clinical event detection, and cross-modality rhythm diagnosis.

error_rate: connection problems reported by 2.8% of respondents; reliability concerns by 3.7%
metric: Technical success rate of ECG transmission/reporting and user-experience survey for a pediatric telecardiology system
result: 158 children screened; ECG transmission and reporting completed successfully in all cases; 90% of respondents were very satisfied or satisfied; 70.8% of respondents completed the full survey.

metric: Survey-based assessment of realism, usability and educational value of an online EP training simulator
result: 90% rated ECG signal realism excellent/very good (82.5% for intracardiac signals); 97.5% would include it in EP training programs; 100% would recommend it.
Conceptual/opinion article applying cognitive load theory to teaching ECG interpretation in paramedical education; no empirical data reported.

metric: Classification accuracy of arousal/valence detection models using video, ECG and EDA data
result: Video-physio models distinguished high/low arousal and valence better than unimodal models, and arousal was classified better than valence; no specific accuracy percentages given. Affective-computing study using ECG only as an ancillary signal, not a cardiology software study.

metric: Accuracy of a CGAN-DBN model identifying flight cadets' cognitive load from multi-source physiological data (eye movement, ECG, respiration)
result: Model reported to achieve 'high accuracy' for cognitive-load identification; no specific accuracy value given in the abstract. Aviation human-factors study using ECG as one of several ancillary signals, not a cardiology software study.

devices: low-cost portable EEG system (27-channel EEG + ECG)
metric: SUS and signal-quality assessment of a low-cost, app-guided portable EEG system used by inexperienced users
result: SUS score 90.3 +/- 6.8 reported by 10 inexperienced users, with an average signal-quality rating of 8.04 and no recordings of insufficient quality; this evaluates an EEG epilepsy-diagnosis system (ECG is only an accompanying channel), not cardiology software.

Describes WACARDIA, free open-source MATLAB/Psychtoolbox software for the heartbeat-detection interoceptive-accuracy task, with a wireless-ECG interface, GUIs, and measurement fail-safes; no quantitative usability or accuracy results reported in the abstract.

metric: Alignment between physiological parameters (EEG, ECG/HRV, GSR) and subjective stress (NASA-TLX) during cobot programming tasks
result: Highest alignment with subjective stress: EEG Theta 76.67%, GSR recovery time 72.86%, HRV PNN25 71.58%; raw RR intervals were least accurate (42.11%). Human-robot collaboration ergonomics study, not a cardiology software study.

metric: Qualitative themes on usability of simplified ECG and audiometry devices among healthcare providers and DR-TB patients
result: 16 healthcare providers and 91 people with drug-resistant tuberculosis were interviewed; providers understood the importance of ECG monitoring but lacked confidence managing the devices and interpreting results; limited device numbers and training were cited as barriers.

metric: Cardiac function (heart rate, R-R interval from ECG) and workload (NASA-TLX) during exoskeleton-assisted gait vs walking without exoskeleton
result: No significant difference in heart rate/R-R ECG data across conditions; NASA-TLX largely unchanged except one comparison. Exoskeleton rehabilitation study using ECG as a safety measure, not a cardiology software study.

metric: Improvement in driver takeover-performance prediction accuracy (GA-BP vs BP neural network) using eye-movement and ECG data
result: At the 10 s time window, the GA-BP model improved accuracy by 5.51%, recall by 7.08%, precision by 6.19% and F1 by 9.71% vs the baseline model. Driving-simulation human-factors study using ECG as an ancillary signal, not a cardiology software study.

metric: Change in HRV metrics (parasympathetic activity) across two weeks of mindfulness practice, experienced (n=20) vs novice (n=26) practitioners
result: Experienced practitioners showed significantly increased, stable parasympathetic activity across practice; novices showed high cognitive load with inconspicuous progressive effects; no specific HRV values reported. A mindfulness/psychophysiology study, not a cardiology software study.

task_time: median 51 minutes per telephone appointment with an ECG technician; average 2.2 attempts to record a usable ECG
error_rate: 2/10 patients unable to obtain a diagnostic-quality ECG
metric: Feasibility and efficiency of home-based 12-lead ECG acquisition prior to a telehealth cardiology appointment
result: 8/10 patients obtained a diagnostic-quality ECG; median technician call time 51 minutes; average 2.2 attempts needed; barriers included internet access, training materials, and motion artifact.
